context_requirements: Expression of a functional nuclear receptor of the steroid receptor superfamily (e.g., NR3C1/GR) in the cell line
Presence of the relevant ligand-binding domain and coactivators (SRC-1/NCOA1, AIB1/NCOA3) for transcriptional activation
For androgen-responsive lines, expression of a functional androgen receptor; VCAP and LNCaP-like lines may have altered ligand specificity
Intact glucocorticoid receptor signaling for dexamethasone-like effects; lines with low NR3C1 may respond weakly
falsifiers: No consistent change in canonical glucocorticoid receptor target genes (e.g., TSC22D3, FKBP4, DUSP1) at 6 h in any line
Absence of any transcriptional response across all nine lines at both 6 h and 24 h
Changes observed only in generic stress or proliferation programs with no receptor-dependent signature
Response in lines lacking NR3C1 expression, which would argue against an NR3C1-mediated mechanism

evidence.supports: Steroid hormones act through a superfamily of nuclear receptors that directly regulate transcription
SRC-1 is a coactivator required for full transcriptional activity of steroid receptors
AIB1/SRC-1 family coactivators enhance steroid receptor-dependent transcription and are amplified in breast/ovarian cancer lines
SRC-1 has histone acetyltransferase activity linking steroid receptor activation to chromatin modification and gene expression
Androgen receptor mutations in LNCaP alter ligand binding and response to steroids and anti-androgens, relevant to VCAP-like prostate lines
